author: CJ Coombs
title: Missing since 2000: Kristopher Charles Loesch was only 10 when he disappeared
text:
2 hours ago Kristopher Charles Loesch. Photo by NCMEC website. Kristopher Charles Loesch has been missing since August 31, 2000, according to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC). He was attending school in Spokane, Washington.
According to The Charley Project , Kristopher was missing from Port Falls, Idaho, where he was last seen in 2001. He is classified as an endangered missing person.
Kristopher's mother and her partner, having been on the run for nearly a decade, ended their lives in Tucson, Arizona. Kristopher may now be in Tucson.
Kristopher's photo above (right) is an age-progressed likeness of how he might have looked at 34, though he would now be 35.
As of today, 204 missing Arizona children are listed with the NCMEC, and the oldest case dates back to 1958. Notably, not all missing children are reported to the NCMEC, but they should be.
About Kristopher Kristopher was only 10 years old when he disappeared. He went missing from his school in Spokane, Washington, on August 31, 2000, but was last known to be in the Pima County, Arizona, area.
Kristopher may use the alias name Robin Kessler or Kristopher Hanson. When Kristopher went missing, he was 5'0" tall and weighed 100 pounds. He has brown hair and blue eyes.
Details Kristopher disappeared with his mother, Tina Rose Loesch (1971-2008) , and her female lover and partner, Skye Marie Hanson (1964-2008) . Tina and Skye were last seen together in Post Falls, Idaho, on May 16, 2001.
Tina's parents were murdered three years apart. Her father, Gary Loesch, was shot to death in 1995 while delivering newspapers. Her mother, Barbara Loesch, was found deceased in a hot tub in her backyard in 1998. Barbara's case was featured in an episode of Oxygen True Crime’s "Accident, Suicide or Murder," titled " Troubled Water ." The episode includes interviews with family members and officials associated with the investigation.
Originally, Barbara's death was ruled an accident. However, in 2004, Bradley Steckman confessed to electrocuting and drowning Barbara. He claimed he was hired by Tina and Skye, who had promised him $10,000 for his role.
Reportedly, after Tina's father died, she began a closer relationship with her mother and influenced her to sign a life insurance policy, making Tina the beneficiary. Tina and Skye later changed their minds about paying Steckman.
When Steckman confessed to Barbara's murder, her husband's case, which is still unsolved, was reopened. It's believed that Tina was involved. When she told her father about her relationship with Skye, he allegedly had her written out of his will.
When Kristopher went missing, he was living with his mother's acquaintance, Steven Cassell, in Spokane Valley, Washington, who was later indicted on charges of illegal money transactions. Kristopher, going by the name of Christopher Robinson, was attending Shiloh Hills Elementary School.
Kristopher, aka Christopher, had stopped attending school and stopped being seen. His school records weren't requested by any potential new school, which indicated he wasn't attending another school. He was supposedly home-schooled by Tina and Skye in 2000 and 2001.
On October 10, 2008, warrants were issued for Tina and Skye's arrests for Barbara's murder. They took off with Kristopher once they learned that Steckman was talking. By November, America's Most Wanted ran a story asking for information on Skye, Tina, and Kristopher's whereabouts.
Less than two hours after the crime show aired, Tina and Skye were found shot to death northwest of Tucson, Arizona. There was no sign of Kristopher at the scene. The women entered into a suicide pact. They left a lengthy suicide note and didn't admit to any involvement in the deaths of Tina's parents. They blamed Steckman for killing Barbara. He died in 2012 while incarcerated, at 44-45.
Kristopher's case remains unsolved. He could be somewhere in the Tucson area. Authorities from Idaho and Arizona have been investigating this case. Reportedly, Kristopher's biological father passed away in 2011.
Kristopher is listed in the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System (NamUs) under case #MP8116 . NamUs is an official website of the U.S. Department of Justice.
If you have any information regarding Kristopher’s disappearance or whereabouts, please call the Pima County Sheriff's Office and reference agency case no. 081115419. You can also call the Post Falls Police at 1-208-773-3517.
You can also contact the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) through its website at https://www.missingkids.org or its 24/7 call center at 1-800-843-5678, and reference NCMEC #986992.
Kristopher has been missing for nearly 26 years. Every missing child's name deserves to be remembered, repeated, and shared until their case is solved. Every renewed search effort makes a difference, and every bit of attention given to a missing child's case helps keep it from growing increasingly cold.
Reporting to the NCMEC The NCMEC is not automatically notified of every missing child, which might explain why the number of missing children sometimes appears low, compared to other statistics. A separate report must be made to the NCMEC, even after law enforcement enters the missing child's information into the FBI's National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database.
When a child is entered into the NCIC database, the information isn't automatically sent to the NCMEC. To activate the NCMEC's resources and support, a separate report must be submitted to them . The NCMEC provides case management, poster distribution, law enforcement assistance, and analytical support.
The number of missing U.S. children fluctuates because many runaways eventually return home. However, some cases involve endangered missing people, endangered runaways, lost or injured missing people, family abductions, non-family abductions, and, unfortunately, foul play is sometimes involved.
Thank you for your time to read and share. Find Kristopher.
